The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.552/19 Police Station New Ashok Nagar, Delhi.
2.
The accident in the present case took place on 13.11.2019.

It is the case of the petitioner that at around 07:00 PM, he was going to Mangal Bazar Road, M.V. -III, Delhi via Kaundali roadside on foot and when he reached at Vidya Bal Bhawan Public School, MIX Housing M.V.-III, offending motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-6SAE-7624, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from the back side and without blowing any horn and applying safety measures, the Ratan Kumar Dass vs Vikram Bhati And Anr.

driver of the offending vehicle hit the petitioner from back side, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Driver managed to flee away from the spot and petitioner was admitted in LBS Hospital wherein MLC was prepared.
3. On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 appeared with IO at the time of filing of DAR.

The respondents no. 1 & 2 who are the driver and owner of the offending motorcycle were given several opportunities to file reply but the same was not availed and their right to file WS was closed on 01.06.2022.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 31.08.2022 : -
(i) Whether the petitioner Mr. Ratan Kumar Das suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 13.11.2019 at about 7:00 pm in front of Vidya Bal Bhawan Public School, MIX Housing M.V.-
III, within the jurisdiction of PS New Ashok Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 6SAE-7624 (motorcycle) by respondent no.1Vikram Bhati ?
(OPP)
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
(iii) Relief 5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Ratan Kumar Das has examined himself as PW-1.
The respondents have not led any evidence.
6. I have heard Ms. Babita Tyagi, Ld. counsel for petitioner and considered the written arguments.
Record has been perused.

7. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1 :Whether the petitioner Mr. Ratan Kumar Das suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 13.11.2019 at about 7:00 pm in front of Vidya Bal Bhawan Public School, MIX Housing M.V.-III, within the jurisdiction of PS New Ashok Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL 6SAE-7624 (motorcycle) by respondent no.1/Vikram Bhati ? (OPP)
8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

sentences.text: Now in this case, the petitioner Ratan Kumar Das is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and tendered in evidence DAR Ex.PW1/2, his aadhar card Ex.PW1/3, Medical Documents Ex.PW1/1, Medical Bills Ex.PW1/4.
He has also placed on record photocopy of Discharge Summary, which is Mark A.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL 6SAE-7624.
He was not cross-examined by the respondents and his testimony remained unassailed.
10. After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1/Vikram Bhati, the driver of the motorcycle.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

sentences.text: 11. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.
12. Respondent no.1
the owner/driver of the offending vehicle did not led any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.

13. It is seen that the driver of the offending vehicle was unknown to the petitioner and had fled away from the spot after the accident and hence his name, does not find a mention in the FIR and further in the testimony of petitioner.

However, chargesheet in the connected criminal case is a part of DAR and it is mentioned therein that the owner of the offending motorcycle Suman Devi was traced out and served a notice under Section 133 M.V. Act and she disclosed that she had sold out the motorcycle to her known Vikram Singh, S/o- Tek Chand and thereafter notice under Section 133 M.V. Act was given to Vikram Singh and he stated that the motorcycle was in his possession being used by him since its purchase from Suman Devi and on 14.11.2019 , while he was driving the offending motorcycle, accident had occurred near Vidya Bal Bhawan, Public School MIX Housing M.V.-III and he had fled away after the accident.
R1 was not subjected to TIP, as criminal case report filed with DAR reflects.
IO filed on record the copy of the notices under Section 133 of the M.V. Act as served to the driver and the registered owner i.e. R1 and R2.
The vehicle was not insured as is clear from the chargesheet, where offence under Section 146/196 M.V. Act was added after R1 failed to produce copy of any insurance certificate before the IO.
In the complaint made to the Police, petitioner has clearly mentioned that he could identify the driver of the offending vehicle.
In the MLC dt. 13.04.2019, alleged history of road traffic accident finds mentioned.

3 RC(part of DAR ) reflects the name of owner as Mrs. Suman Devi.

sentences.text: The copy of notices under Section 133 M.V. Act are not filed with the DAR, nonetheless, chargesheet makes it clear that R1 was in possession of offending motorcycle and driving the same at the time of accident.
Further, at the stage of Final Arguments, IO filed on record the copies of notices under Section 133 M.V. Act, as specified in the charge-sheet.
During investigation in the criminal case, IO recorded statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C of petitioner on the point of identification of R1, which is attached to the DAR.

In the license of R1, his name is reflected as Vikram Singh and IO clarified in writing that surname of Vikram Singh is 'Bhati' and hence, the same finds mentioned at some point in charge-sheet and that Vikram Singh and Vikram Bhati is the same person.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and from filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner Ratan Kumar Das received injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Vikram Singh @ Vikram Bhati, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if yes, to what extent and from
whom?(OPP)
15. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

Now, in the present case, the injured Ratan Kumar Das has suffered from fracture and as per radiology opinion, there was 'fracture distal end radius left side' and the nature of injuries was opined as griveous.

4 has also deposed regarding swelling and defomity on his left wrist.

sentences.text: Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
17.
Petitioner has proved some of his medical bills.
Under this head, actual medical bills are reimbursed.

The bills which are on record are of Rs.47,896/- ( Ld. Counsel for petitioner has filed bill summary and at Sl. No. 1 mentioned the bill amount of bill dt. 26.11.2019 as Rs.560/- but the bill on record, part of Ex.PW1/4 no. 0029950 dt. 26.11.2019 reflects the total amount as Rs.1560/- and further it is seen that the bill dt. 09.04.2019 pertains to some purchase made by Counsel for the petitioner Ms. Babita Tyagi from LRC Publications for a sum of Rs.500/- and is not any medical bill of petitioner and further the invoice no. 47 which is part of Ex.PW1/4 for a sum of Rs.2108.85/- is a photocopy but is also part of the DAR (where IO has filed copy of the same bill with stamp of Dr.
Sanjeev Tripathi and signature of SHO regarding verification).
Alongwith the DAR, IO has placed on record one Bill of petitioner Sl. No.50 dt. 12.01.2020 for Rs.200,.
Therefore, I award Rs.47,396/-+Rs.2108/-+Rs.200/- = Total Rs.49,704/- as compensation under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
18.
There is nothing in the testimony or original medical documents of petitioner to suggest that he remained hospitalized for any given period.

However, petitioner has relied on document Mark A suggesting his admission on 20.11.2019 and discharge on 21.11.2019, under consultation of Dr.
Sanjeev Tripathi.
He is the same doctor, some documents pertaining to whom have been verified by the IO.

Further the MLC of petitioner reflects the date of his arrival in LBS Hospital on 13.11.2019 and even if he was discharged on the same date, it can be safely assumed that he remained admitted in hospital in connection with medical treatment post accident for a day.
He is stated to be having swelling in deformity on left wrist and abression on right lower limb and was suggested fore-arm Xray.
Further, as per the opinion of Radiologist, he sustained 'fracture distal and radius left side'.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, petitioner must have remained under pain and suffering for days.
Therefore, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.10,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and special diet charges.
20. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or Ratan Kumar Dass vs Vikram Bhati And Anr. on 26 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177589666/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5 would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
21. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.10,000/- (5,000+5,000) under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :

22. Petitioner has claimed that he was working as Production Incharge in Leather Goods at A-10,
Sector 64, Noida, U.P. and was getting salary of Rs.28,000/- per month.
He has not placed on record copy of his salary slip or bank statement reflecting his employment and salary.
However, IO has placed on record with the DAR salary slip of the respondent of month November 2019 and the same reflects the date of his joining as 05.11.2019.
No other salary slip has been filed by the IO.
IO has also not mentioned anywhere that this bill was verified by the Departments and prior to 05.11.2019, where was the petitioner working and what was his salary.
No appointment letter has been filed on record either.
No ITR has been filed and no education qualification of petitioner has been divulged by him.
However, there is no contrary evidence against this by the respondents.
There is no harm in believing that the petitioner must have been earning this much money as claimed by him in his testimony.
Therefore, his income is taken as Rs.28,000/- per month.
The evidence of the petitioner shows that he remained hospitalized for around 1 day.
Petitioner, though did not specify how long he remained on bed, it can be assumed that he must have remained indoors on account of the accident or about 1 month.
Otherwise also it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture he must have been disabled from work for a least a month as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Therefore, I award Rs.28,000/- as compensation under this head.

23. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarised as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1 Medical Expenses Rs.49,704/-
 2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.10,000/-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.5,000/-
 4 Attendant charges Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of Income during Rs.28,000/-
 treatment  TOTAL Rs.97,704/-
Issue No. 3 (iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP)

sentences.text: Petitioner has pursued his case diligently.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 8% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
25.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
In the case at hand, R2 is the registered owner of the vehicle, which was not insured on the date of offence.
She has failed to bring on record any document in proof of the sale of her motorcycle to R1.
Hence, as registered owner of the vehicle, she cannot be absolved of her liability towards the victim.
It is also seen that R1 has admitted in his reply to the IO that the vehicle was in his actual possession and ownership, having purchased the same from R2.
He has not lead any evidence in the present case, despite him being impleaded as one of the respondents.
Respondent No.1 is the driver of the vehicle and was driving the same at the time of accident.
The liability of respondents no. 1 and 2 who are the driver and the registered owner is joint and several.

RELIEF:
26.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.97,704/- (Rs. Ninety Seven Thousands, Seven Hundred and Four only) along with interest @ 8% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.1/Vikram Singh @ Vikram Bhati and R2/Suman Devi.
Both of them are held jointly and sevarally liable for payment of the award amount alongwith interest.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
Announced in the open Mayuri Singh Court on 26.07.2023 Presiding Officer-MACT (East)
